# OLYMPUS v0.0.19, "Stack and clear: the rest of the kit, the team, the first live men": the build sheet

> This is the round's build sheet as written before the build (2026-11-16), kept whole as the contract the roles built to, with §14 added after the build: the round's resolutions. §14 wins over any line above it that it contradicts. DESIGN.md's log of 2026-11-16 carries the decisions. Where the sheet says v0.0.17's lines or a `// (v0.0.19 …)` anchor, the lead strips those anchors before the release.


Written 2026-11-16 for the round's seven implementers and the lead, who integrates. It is the contract between roles that build in parallel without talking. It sits on v0.0.18 as `.run/v018-design/sheet.md` gives it; where v0.0.18 as built differs from its sheet, the code decides and the role says so in its handoff.

Where this sheet is silent, the docs decide: DESIGN.md and the user's rules first, then TECH §1.3, then the sections it cites, then the three designs (kit2, team, opfor, as handed to this sheet). My own choices are marked (my call). Every conflict between the three designs, and between them and v0.0.18, is settled in §0.

**Lines.** Every file:line is v0.0.17's (`3c3a512`), checked read-only, unless it says "D1 as built" (the v0.0.18 kit worktree `.claude/worktrees/v018-kit`, read on 2026-11-16, in progress). v0.0.18's merges move most of them (bundle.js alone gains about 400 lines), so **every hunk is named by its function**, and the line is only a pointer.

**The release.** The shoot house stays the pilot (the user, 2026-11-11: "This mission should be perfected before you spend any token on any other mission"). Three tracks, in order of priority:

1. **K, the kit's second slice (D2)**: practice frag and concussion grenades (G-9P, G-13P) scored by the instructor as live ones; the BC-1 hinge-side cutting charge on the pull door; the R-7's ballistic breach; the planner over devices. The user's ask of 2026-11-15 ("breaching options and equipment (explosives etc), and grenades (bangs, frags, concussion etc)"), finished.
2. **T, the team**: role and side kept apart, the other side (FM 3-06.11 §3-29), the #2's stoppages from his belief through v0.0.18's planner, the team's words in one table, the #2's P-12 behind one switch (off), and "#2, bang it" / "Breacher up" / "As you were".
3. **L, the first live men**: two role-players in place of stands 2a and 3a, on their own scored scene, "Stack and clear, live" (`test-shoothouse-live`). This is COMBAT §25.18's reach review's prerequisites of `test-breach`, built in the pilot (§0 item 17).

**Merge order**: stage 0 (the lead), then K (K-sim, then K-face), then T, then L (men, opfor, house, look). **Ship rule** (my call): K and T ship in v0.0.19. L ships if its suites and LIVE_ENFORCED are green on the last merge; otherwise nothing of L reaches main and it follows as v0.0.20, so the user's two finished asks never wait on the third.

**If v0.0.18 ships without its kit** (its sheet allows it, §0 and §8 item 17 there): v0.0.19 is D1 plus T0 to T3 plus L on the standard loadout; K and T's stage T4 become v0.0.20, and every D1 name below is re-read against what was built before any role starts.

**What the user must feel.**
- From the picker, "Kit: Frag" puts two G-9Ps on the carrier. The instructor's brief says which rooms are hostiles only. At room 1, "Frag, in: your corner" is a row: "Frag out!", the stack on the wall, a pop and a puff, the instructor's "Good frag. 1a and 1b down.", the stands turned away by his hand, the entry.
- A frag into room 2 or room 3 is a fault every time, with the instructor's "You never frag a family."
- At room 2's pull door, with "Kit: Cut", the BC-1 goes on the hinge side, the stack backs 3.18 m down the latch-side wall, "Breaching!", and the leaf is blown in.
- At the closet, on a breaching loadout, "Shoot the lock": real rounds from the magazine, 45 degrees down and in.
- When you take your #2's side of a room, he takes yours, calling "Left!" or "Right!" as the screen names it.
- "#2, bang it": he goes to the front, throws, steps back, and you lead in.
- On "Stack and clear, live", the man in room 2's deep corner is a man: he turns to the door, aims at it, fires marking pairs, gives up or hides on his card, and goes down sitting, still armed, until you or your #2 cover him.

**The user's rules hold over every section:** we only know what we know (the planners read the belief; the instructor's read of a practice grenade is the truth, shown after the burst, never before; a live man is known through the take-in); never a dead end; nothing pops in or out of view; AZERTY labels on physical codes; every image and sound by code; one loadout for every sheet; no overlapping UI; the standard lane is v0.0.18's to the byte unless this sheet names the change.

**Kept as built and starred:** "Bang" (scored 100 on 2026-11-15) and its four B goldens; P3-j's band; the tower's macros and their words; the row ids every bot, the instinct and the gauges key on; F1 to F26, never loosened.

**Rules of the round:**
- Edit only your own files and named hunks (§1). Report any other edit needed, exactly, in your handoff.
- No commits, tags, pushes, releases or promotions. Never touch `.play/`, :8200, :8201, `../longhaul` or `../tradecraft`.
- Scratch goes under `/private/tmp/claude-501/olympus-build/v019/<role>/`. Your handoff goes in `.run/v019/<role>.md` (it survives a reboot): CHANGELOG bullets, doc text, the figures before and after, every edit outside your list, the stubs you tested against.
- Worktrees: `git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/v019-<role> v0.0.18`, then `git -C <wt> apply .run/v019/stage0.patch` (§2).
- Seven roles share the machine: run the runner with `JOBS=2` (my call; 7 × 2 workers is the machine's half), and only `QUICK=1` or a file with its separator (`'house-frag ›'`). Heavy suites wait for the lead's quiet-machine run (§9). While `lsof -nP -iTCP:8200 -sTCP:LISTEN` answers, `JOBS=1`.

**Ports:** T 8230, K-sim 8231, K-face 8232, L-men 8233, L-opfor 8234, L-house 8235, lead 8236, L-look 8237, reviews 8238 and 8239 (`OLYMPUS_TEST_PORT` for single browser suites; the runner claims 8240 to 8249 itself). Kill every server you start.

**Interfaces first.** Each role writes §3's exports as stubs with the shapes given, then fills them, and tests against its own stub of another role's module until that role merges.

**Integration.** The stage-0 tree is the base: `B=$(cat .run/v019/base.tree)`. Each role's patch is

```
git -C <wt> add -N . && git -C <wt> diff $B > .run/v019/<role>.patch
```

(`git diff` against a tree object works with intent-to-add files: checked in scratch, 2026-11-16). The lead applies them with `git apply --3way` in the merge order, running `QUICK=1 node tests/run.mjs` after each. Before its final run, each role rebases onto the integrated tree the roles before it left (`git -C <wt> checkout -- . && git -C <wt> apply <integrated.patch>`, then its own on top with `--3way`).

## 0. What the cross-check found (verified; each settled here)

**Against D1 as built (the kit worktree, in progress):**

1. **D1's shapes differ from kit2's reading in seven places.** Each is settled for D2:
   - `R.house.broken[door]` holds the burst's ms (`burst.js` step 4), not a word. D2 keeps it a ms and writes the method on `R.house.breach[door].how` ('charge' | 'cut' | 'shot' | 'pry' | 'ram'), never in `broken`.
   - The believed fuse is `devices.js fuseBelieved(model)` (the band's bottom, 4,000 ms), not a field of `deviceBelief`. devplan.js reads it there.
   - `throw.js throwSolve` already takes `fuseMs` and picks the throw against it. D2's throw.js hunk is `aimOf` and passing the fuse left after a cook, nothing in the solver.
   - `BREACH_SAFE_KPA` 27.6 and `STUN_KPA` 20 live in `blast.js`, not breach.js.
   - `kitHas(state, pid, 'charge')` knows only the SC-1. D2 adds the need `'cut'` (a BC-1 and an FD-1) and `'frag'`, `'conc'`, `'ballistic'`.
   - `DEVICE_STATES` has no 'misfire' or 'fired'. They are added, additively, absent meaning the first state as D1 has it.
   - `blast.js fragHits(seed, burstId, pid, lambda)` exists, on the stream `'arms:frag'`. practice.js draws its fragments through it (with the stand's key in `pid`'s place), never a stream of its own: one helper for one quantity.
2. **D1's `burst()` dazes every stand in the burst's room by a startle, whatever the model** (`burst.js` step 3, `DAZED_FACES`), so a 4 g spotting charge would daze the stands and kit2's read would daze them again. Settled: for a model with `DEVICES[model].as`, step 3 is skipped and the read alone sets the stands' daze (`T.dazeUntilMs` from the read's `stunMs`). One source.
3. **supp.js's 'blast' input ignores the charge's size** (`supp.js:236`: by range alone), so a practice grenade's pop gives the stack the live G-9's points. Settled (my call): kept, since the stack is prepared by the call and a practice day is loud; the risk is in §10. No supp.js edit this round.
4. **D1's burst already prepares the whole stack when a man of the stack throws and calls** (`burst.js stackOf`: `byId` in the stack and `called` gives the stack). team's burst.js hunk ("prepared by a teammate's Bang out!") is dropped: it is already so.
5. **kit2's figures re-run on D1's own `blast.js`** (scratch `check-blast.mjs`): the G-9 at #1's room 1 point 17.4 kPa (deep throw) and 34.9 (centre); the BC-1's stand-off 3.18 m at 66 kPa, 3.46 at 101.3, **1.71** in Mars' surface air (kit2: 1.70); the G-13's closed-room pressure 13.7, 10.0 and 152.7 kPa (room 1, room 2, the closet). Two differ: a G-13 at room 2's centre puts **35.8 kPa** on 2b (kit2: 37), and room 3's hostage takes **9.3 kPa** (kit2: 10). 2b's margin over `EARDRUM_KPA` 34.5 is 1.3 kPa, so "a concussion at room 2's centre injures the no-shoot" turns on a threshold marked "to check". The tests quote D1's numbers and print the margin.

**Between the three designs:**

6. **The new gauges collide**: kit2's F30 to F33, team's F30 to F33 and opfor's F30 to F36. Renumbered by merge order (§8): K F30 to F33, T F34 to F37, L F38 to F44.
7. **"Who throws and breaches" is built twice**: kit2's `KIT_BY` in breach.js with MUSCLE rows `team:bang` and `team:breacher` (`offeredNow: false`), and team's `DOER_DEFAULT` in team.js with `team:bang`, `team:breach` and `team:belay`, live. **team's is kept.** kit2 drops `KIT_BY` and its two team rows. kit2's new beats carry `slots: [1]` as D1's do, and T converts every kit beat (D1's and K's) to `doer: true` on its rebase (team §6).
8. **"The #2 takes the other side when blocked" is read three ways.** team reads it as FM 3-06.11 §3-29's other side when you take his: that is the question's switch, `TEAM_OPPOSITE` in team.js. kit2's `TWO_SIDE_BLOCKED` is about where the #2 waits for a charge when the latch-side wall is short: a different thing, renamed `CHARGE_SIDE_SHORT` ('same' | 'other', default 'same') so the two cannot be confused. opfor's `blockedBy` (a defender on a point) is not built: slice 1 places no role-player on a point or a path, and `opfor-spots` holds it.
9. **`breach.js safePointsOf` is extended twice** (kit2's `{ edge, side }`, team's `{ by }`). K owns it: `safePointsOf(state, plan, model = 'sc1', { side = CHARGE_SIDE_SHORT } = {})`, the stand-off measured from the charge's own edge (D1's `chargePointOf` grows a `side: 'latch' | 'hinge'`). team's `by` is dropped: the doer takes `one`, and the other man stands on the give line, `team.js giveOf(plan, one)`.
10. **`loadout.js` is edited twice** (kit2's presets, team's `~two:p12`). K owns it and builds team's token as team specifies: `spec.two = { p12: TWO_P12_DEFAULT }` (false), `codeOf` appends `~two:p12` only when true (after a preset's name or a `v1` code), and `loadoutOf` strips it first. Every v0.0.18 code round-trips byte for byte.
11. **`shoothouse.js` is edited by all three** (kit2's hunks, team's hunks, opfor's house role "owned whole"). Settled:
    - Stage 0 (the lead) moves the #2's code to `house-two.js` byte for byte (team's T0) and plumbs ownership through `team.js` stubs (item 14), before any role starts.
    - K and T keep their logic in their own modules (K: `house-kit.js`, new; T: `team.js`, `house-two.js`), and their shoothouse.js hunks are call lines and table entries under their anchors (§2).
    - L-house owns the rest of the file, and merges last.
12. **The cycle `shoothouse.js` ↔ `house-two.js` can throw at load.** shoothouse re-exports house-two's names, and house-two imports shoothouse's (houseOf, curLeg, planOf, noteSighting, houseShot, chiefSays, whole, actorOf). Function references are safe in a cycle; a top-level read of a binding is a TDZ error whichever module loads first. Checked: the moved block's top level reads `CALL_S` (bundle.js) and `COURSES` (via `C`, shoothouse.js:159). Rule: **house-two.js reads no shoothouse.js binding at its top level**; it imports `CALL_S` from bundle.js and `COURSES` from courses.js itself. A stage-0 test loads each of house-two.js, devplan.js and shoothouse.js first in a fresh process.
13. **"seenK reproduces today's expression bit for bit" is not one expression.** contact.js:178, shoothouse.js:862 and :1038 quantise (`q(sightOf(…).vis * f, 1e-6)`), contact.js:420 (`twoOn`) does not. Settled: `men.js seenK` returns the raw product for a turner, and each call site keeps its own `q()` or none. The `men` test holds every site's value equal to v0.0.18's on every tick of a tier-one lane.
14. **Ownership is read in 14 places, not through one reader**:
    - contact.js 209, 230, 244 and 306 (`T.slot`);
    - contact.js 406 (`hisOnly`, `manPlace(state, T).slot`);
    - bundle.js 679 (the call kind's `up`), 1129 (`upPick`'s `mine`) and 1138 (`mineUp`);
    - cqb.js 184, 187, 192, 390 and 405;
    - shoothouse.js 859, 860, 929 and 984 (the #2's).
    team (T1) and live (the house role) both rewrite them. Settled: **stage 0 does the plumbing**. `team.js` is created with `ownerOf(state, T)` returning `T.slot` exactly as each site reads it, and `roleAt(state, door, side)` returning `side`. Every site calls them, byte-identical on every lane (the pin, §2). Then T fills the real bodies and L only calls them. The two meanings are kept apart:
    - `T.slot` is the side, the geometry. opfor writes it from `room.js manPlace` for live records only.
    - `ownerOf` is the role.
    (Sites 859, 929 and 984 read `T.slot === 1` while the others read `(T.slot ?? 1)`. Every stand has a slot, so they agree; the stub keeps each site's own form.)
15. **The #2's sighting and his ownership sit on adjacent lines** (shoothouse.js 859 to 862, and :1038), which T and L both edit. Stage 0 pulls them into two one-line helpers in house-two.js, `twoOwns(state, T)` and `twoSees(state, a, T, now)` (byte-identical). T edits `twoOwns`, and L edits `twoSees`.
16. **The standard lane must not move by accident.** D1 already rules that "the standard makes nothing and writes nothing" (its fill, D1 as built). v0.0.19 extends that to every new field: absent means the default. Settled:
    - kit2's `H.five` is written only on a lane whose loadout carries a charge or a tool, and `R.house.intel` only when the loadout carries a G-9P or G-13P.
    - **Shoot the lock is offered only on those breaching lanes** (`BALLISTIC_LANES` 'breach', my call). kit2's extra fan row at the closet on the standard loadout is gone, and with it kit2's risk 5 and test 34's exception.
    - team's `H.two.side`, `H.two.task` and `H.two.pistol` are written only when used. opfor writes nothing with `opfor` none.
    - **Two changes move the standard lane, on purpose, both team's**: the #2's drill from his belief (`twoFixOf`, item 20), and your Cover his sector saying "Covering!" first (200 ms). They move only lanes where the #2 has a stoppage. The shared pin is re-recorded at T's merge with every moved cell printed (§2, §9).
17. **The live lane against the ROADMAP's order.** ROADMAP §4.2 puts `test-zerocqb` (0.0.7e) before `test-breach` (0.0.7f). The user's priority of 2026-11-11 keeps every token in the shoot house, and `test-zerocqb` is another mission. Settled (my call): the role-players are built in house 1 as their own scored scene. "Stack and clear" itself is untouched (with no `&opfor`, nothing of L runs), and `test-breach`'s one-room scene is later re-cut from it. Logged for the user to overrule.
18. **Two optional issues both claim to be "the last items of the fill".** Settled, in this order:
    1. v0.0.18's (your P-12, your loadout, then his);
    2. the #2's P-12 (`~two:p12`);
    3. the role-players (`opfor`).
    Each is absent by default, so every default id is v0.0.18's.
19. **Faults named twice.**
    - D1's `blast` ("the stack in the blast") already is kPa ≥ 27.6 on a man of the stack. It now holds for any device: one quantity, one fault. kit2's `burst` fault means fragments on a man of the stack (n ≥ 1) and its cease fire only.
    - kit2's `blasted` (a no-shoot injured by a G-13) is renamed `concussed`, beside D1's `blast`.
    - L's lane end 'casualty' and K's 'burst' are both cease-fire ends with their card.
20. **team's `twoFixOf` is right and overdue.** `twoDrillOf` (shoothouse.js:1000) reads `gunField(gun, 'jam')` and `mag.n`, the truth. With v0.0.18's `planFor(state, pid, gunId, goal, { carry, look, purpose })` (the arms worktree, plan.js:375) the #2 plans from his belief as you do.
21. **devplan.js must not import combat/.** `breach.js` imports `bundle.js` (D1 as built, breach.js:30), and plan.js would import devplan.js through guard 0. So devplan.js imports only `arms/devices.js`, `arms/kit.js`, `arms/carry.js`, `combat/roll.js` and core. The actor's place against the door (`at`) is passed in by the caller (bundle.js, the panel), and plan.js's guard 0 needs only the hands.
22. **The live lane's marking rounds cannot breach.** Shoot the lock is struck 'marking rounds' there (my call).
23. **A practice frag on a live man** never turns him away: `readsTick` leaves `T.live` records alone (K), and L, on its rebase, makes them call `opfor.ruleOut(state, bus, T, 'frag')`. The honest bots never frag rooms 2 or 3 (2b and 3b are always noncombatants: STANDS, shoothouse.js:200-205), so this is the fuzz's case.
24. **`tests/flawless.mjs` would be edited by four parties.** Stage 0's hunk lets `botOf` take a factory and `flawlessLane` take `fill` (spread into `createGame`). No track edits flawless.mjs, so F1 to F26 cannot move by construction.
25. **Breach on 5 moves keys on v0.0.18's own breach and full lanes** (they carry charges or tools, so `H.five` is 'breach' there). That is the P3 pick the user drew. v0.0.18's kit-lane panel pins are re-pinned and said, never loosened.
26. **The quick suite's 60 s ceiling** (it was 32.8 s at v0.0.16, 1,071 tests). About 30 new quick files are coming. Rule: a quick file stays under 3 s of CPU, and any whole lane is heavy, unless it is one sheet on one seed.

## 3. Interfaces

### 3.1 K-sim

**`devplan.js`** (pure; imports per item 21). Exports: `DEV_GOALS` ('thrown', 'placed', 'fired', 'clear'), `DEV_POPS` 200, `DEV_PLANS_MAX` 1,024, and:

```js
devAbsOf(state, pid, itemId, { at = 'far' } = {}) → DevAbs   // kit2 §2.2's shape; `at` from the caller
devKey(abs), stepDev(abs, act) → DevAbs | null
devPlan(abs, goal) → { goal, path, costMs, none? }
devPlanFor(state, pid, itemId, goal, { at }) → { …, id, label, ms }
handsPath(state, pid) → { path, ms, label } | null          // null: the hands hold no device
devNameOf(path, model, goal) → { id, label }
devReachable(), clearDevPlans()
```

- The guards are kit2's D1 to D3: a live grenade offers only Throw and Throw it clear; 'clear' never throws an armed grenade; a believed misfire waits `MISFIRE_WAIT_MS` with a counting badge.
- The edges are D1's `DEVICE_EDGES` plus `D2_EDGES` (devices.js).
- It reads `fuseBelieved`, never `fuseMs` or `misfire`'s truth.

**plan.js guard 0**: in `planFor`, for the goals fire, fed, retain and topup, a non-null `handsPath` is prepended. `nameOf` names a path that opens with a device act by `devNameOf`.

**`practice.js`** (pure):

```js
readBurst(state, { burst, model, x, z, atMs, room }) → Read
fragLine(state, area, from, to) → { keeps, through: [opening] }
ballVMs(rM, air), ballPenMm(vMs)
throwExposure(state, pid, { fromMs, toMs, door })
readMarks(read) → [{ text, fault }]
PRACTICE_CONST
```

- Every wall of `places/plan.js wallsOf` stops every ball: the house's ballistic panels (PLACES table, 10 mm steel faced with 50 mm rubber). It is a rule of practice.js, `WALL_STOPS`, not a new `penetrate.js` material.
- A closed leaf is `penetrate.js pStop` on `LEAF_WALL` (WALLS.cabin), keyed by the opening's kind.
- Fragments come through `blast.js fragHits`.

**The Read** (on `R.house.bursts[i].read`, written by `burst()` for a model with `as`):

```
{ model, as, x, z, atMs, room, kPaRoom,
  stands: { [T.key]: { stand, face, rM, lam, n, kPa, out: 'down'|'wounded'|'stunned'|'injured'|null, stunMs } },
  stack: { me: { rM, lam, n, kPa }, two: { … } }, noncombatants: [stand], fragged: bool, concussed: [stand],
  exposed: { ms, by: [stand] } | null, uncookedMs: number | null, applied?: true }
```

- `T.hits` entries are `{ by: 'frag', burst: <item id>, n, part: null }`. The field is `burst`, never `burstId` (ids-check :29).
- `T.downBy` is 'g9' | 'g13'.

**`ballistic.js`** (pure):

```js
BREACH_POINTS, shootPlanOf(state, pid, plan) → { how: 'lock'|'hinge', points: [{ key, yM }] }
pitchOf(grade, rng), defeatOf(how, grade, rng), throughLeaf(r, round), strikeLine(state, { from, yawRad, pitchRad, door })
shootRound(state, bus, d, point) → { shot, defeated, struck: stand | null }
```

- Each round is `shot.js resolveShot` with `target: { kind: 'door', door, dM: 0.05 }`, `part: 'thing'` and `row: { id: 'shoot:door' }`, so the magazine, a stoppage and the dummy all run as for any shot.
- `R.house.breach[door] = { how, rounds, points, atMs }`.

**`house-kit.js`** (new; imports practice.js, never burst.js, so there is no cycle):
- `readsTick(state, bus, R, H, now)`: kit2 §2.4, skipping `T.live`;
- `intelOf(state)` → `{ [door]: 'hostiles' | 'unknown' }`, or null;
- `fiveOf(state)` → 'breach' | null;
- `kitMarks(state, H, L)`;
- `breachShot(state, bus, shot)`.

**The house record** (all absent by default):
- `R.house.intel` and `R.house.five` ('breach' only; absent is Enter on 5);
- `R.house.breach`;
- `L.throws: [{ by, atMs, exposedMs, at }]`.

## 10. Risks (each owned)

- **D1 slipping** (lead): §0's opening rule.
- **The startle suspension** (L-men) applies to every startle on every house lane. On D1's flash lanes the stack's own bang is prepared, so F27 should not move; the pin's flash lanes print it, and a move is explained, never loosened.
- **Breach on 5** (K-face) moves Enter off the five on breaching lanes: 27 of the honest bot's 54 door stops pressed it (groups.js:141's comment). It is a lane constant. Question 4 asks.
- **The live men's balance** (L-house): the recruit may often end 'casualty' in room 3 (the role-player there sees #1 first). F44 and `live-race` print it by sheet before anything is tuned. Question 8 asks.
- **'unaccounted' can hold a Clear** while a man hides where the drill does not look (L-house). The safeguards: `opfor-spots`, `CLEAR_HOLD_MS`'s hand-back and "Find him".
- **The art scope** (L-look): a rifle leaving his hands undrawn would pop. F43 and `ui-live` fail on it. The look samples' defaults land even if scoring waits.
- **The thresholds marked "to check"**: `CORNER_SHADOW_K`, the eardrum and lung thresholds, the hinge placement, `MISFIRE_WAIT_MS`, three hinges, rifle ballistic breaching, and FM 3-06.11 §3-29's wording. Each is one constant; the DESIGN log lists them.
- **Practice sounds as practice**: a pop and a puff. The user may expect a bang: the live twin is drawn and said, never played (my call, honest).
- **A cook never bursts in the hand** (3.35 s worst against a 4.0 s fuse). That danger would need a longer cook than WEAPONS allows.
- **Seven roles on one machine**: `JOBS=2`, and heavy suites only for the lead.

## 13. For the user

**The open questions, each built with its default and one switch:**

| Question | Built default | The one switch |
|---|---|---|
| Does your #2 carry a P-12? | No (he would carry 1.21 kg more; MAKE READY 3.6 s and SHOW CLEAR 6.1 s longer at the private, beside your own; the pistol, not Gun down, at a jam with a man facing within 10 m) | `TWO_P12_DEFAULT` (loadout.js), or `~two:p12` on the picker |
| Does he take the other side when you take his? | Yes, as FM 3-06.11 has it, called "Left!" or "Right!"; never while you stand in the doorway, where he holds and says "Coming in!" as now | `TEAM_OPPOSITE` (team.js) |
| Who throws and breaches? | You, as #1; your #2 on your word ("#2, bang it", "Breacher up", TEAM 2 and 3) | `DOER_DEFAULT` (team.js) |
| Frag and concussion grenades? | Practice grenades in the house, scored by the instructor as live ones would have done | `PRACTICE_ISSUED` (loadout.js) |
| "Bang"? | Unchanged | (none touched) |

**The questions this round raises (only the real ones):**

1. **Ballistic breaching.** Should the R-7 with the house's frangible be the house's ballistic breach now, slow and poor as doctrine says of rifle rounds, with a B-12 breaching shotgun later? Or should ballistic breaching wait for the B-12? *Default: the R-7 now, on breaching lanes only.*
2. **A practice frag's would-have.** When the instructor's read says a frag would have put a stand down, should he turn it away, so the lane plays as a live frag would have? Or should every stand stay up to be shot, with the read only on the run sheet? *Default: turned away.*
3. **When a frag is wrong.** The brief names the rooms that hold hostiles only, and a frag or concussion into any other room is a fault, whatever it would have hit. Or should a grenade be judged only by what it would have hit? *Default: the brief's word, as doctrine has it.*
4. **Key 5 at a door.** On a lane whose kit carries a charge or a tool, AT THE DOOR's key 5 is Breach, as your P3 pick drew it, and Enter moves to the fan. Or should Enter stay on 5 on every lane? *Default: Breach on 5 on breaching lanes, fixed for the whole lane.*
5. **Swapped sides on the run sheet.** When you take your #2's side and he takes yours, should the run sheet count it as a fault against your corner rule, or note it? *Default: noted, "SIDES SWAPPED".*
6. **Who leads after "#2, bang it".** Your #2 works the door from the front while you wait half a pace into the hall, then you go in first. Or should the man who opened the door lead? *Default: you lead.*
7. **Paint on the live lane.** Two in the chest or one on the mask, on you or on your #2: should the lane end there with its card, or carry on one-man as a casualty drill? *Default: the lane ends, with the card.*
8. **The role-players' quality.** The same security-grade opponent on every run, so "Again as …" compares sheets fairly, or drawn by the seed from an insurgent up to enemy special forces? *Default: the same on every run.*
9. **A man who gave up, shot.** Judged on what the shooter could see at that round: a fault on the card, as a hit no-shoot is, or the lane's end, as the career will treat it? *Default: a fault on the card.*

**Samples to score:** `samples/opfor-look` (masks M1 to M3, hands H1 and H2, paint P1 and P2). Defaults are drawn until you pick.
